subject: geography
status_note: Topic structure checked against the WAEC (WASSCE) Geography syllabus as published in a third-party copy of the official text, and against schemes of work that describe themselves as following the NERDC senior secondary curriculum. The official NERDC curriculum document was not available to us. World Explorer is not approved or endorsed by WAEC or NERDC.

sections.title: Practical geography and map work
sections.waec: Part A: map work, statistical maps and diagrams, GIS (GIS is examined for Nigeria only)

topics.title: Map reading: scale, distance, reduction and enlargement
Direction, bearing and representation of relief
Interpretation of physical and cultural features on maps
GIS data, satellite remote sensing and applications

sections.title: Physical geography
sections.waec: Part A: the earth in space, rocks, tectonic and denudational processes, landforms, weather and climate, climate change (Nigeria only), the environment

topics.title: The earth in space: solar system, rotation, revolution, latitude, longitude and time
Structure of the earth and rocks
Earth's internal processes: earth movements, vulcanicity and earthquakes
Running water, groundwater, wind and waves: processes and landforms
Weather: elements, instruments and the weather station
Climate: controls, types and classification (Greek and Köppen)

sections.title: Human and economic geography
sections.waec: Part B: world population, settlement, transportation, industry, trade, tourism

topics.title: Settlement: rural and urban, functions and interactions

sections.title: Regional geography of Nigeria
sections.waec: Part C (Nigeria): broad outline, physical setting, population, resources, agriculture, transportation, communication, industry, trade, tourism, development and environmental issues, ECOWAS, geopolitical issues

topics.title: Location and Physical Setting of Nigeria
Local geography: your town or village and local government area

sections.title: Fieldwork
sections.waec: Part D: one fieldwork study (land use, market survey, traffic flow, journey to work or local erosion), assessed in school

topics.title: Planning and reporting a fieldwork study

not_for_nigeria: Elementary surveying, hydrosphere, vegetation and soil (as world topics) are marked in the WAEC syllabus for Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia and The Gambia. Nigeria's vegetation and soils are covered in Lesson 3 as part of Nigeria's physical setting.
The regional geography of Ghana, Sierra Leone, Liberia, Senegambia and the selected topics on Africa are examined for those countries, not for Nigerian candidates.
